name: Itanagar
description: Capital city of Arunachal Pradesh and major urban centre in Papum Pare district. Gateway with airport, markets, and base for exploring nearby heritage and nature sites including Ita Fort and Ganga Lake.
facts: State capital of Arunachal Pradesh
Named after Ita Fort (Fort of Bricks)
Elevation around 320 m
Connected by Donyi Polo Airport and Naharlagun railway

name: Ita Fort
description: Medieval brick fort ruins in Itanagar that give the capital its name. Built in the 14th-15th century, likely by Sutiya/Chutia kings, with irregular walls, three gateways, and archaeological significance.
facts: Name means 'Fort of Bricks' in Assamese
Total brickwork about 16,200 cubic metres
Three gateways: western, eastern, southern
Finds displayed at Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum

name: Ganga Lake (Gyakar Sinyi)
description: Serene natural freshwater lake about 6 km from Itanagar, locally called Gyakar Sinyi meaning 'confined water'. Surrounded by forest within Itanagar Wildlife Sanctuary; popular for boating, picnics and birdwatching.
facts: About 6 km west of Itanagar city centre
Local Nyishi name Gyakar Sinyi / Geker Sinying
Lies within Itanagar Wildlife Sanctuary
Associated with local folklore involving mithun

name: Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum
description: State museum in Itanagar showcasing ethnographic collections of Arunachal tribal cultures including costumes, jewellery, weapons, handicrafts and archaeological artefacts from sites like Ita Fort.
facts: Established in the 1980s; new building inaugurated 1990
Ground floor ethnographic dioramas; first floor archaeology
Includes cane workshop and handicraft shop
Located near Gompa on Museum Road

name: Gompa Buddhist Temple (Centre for Buddhist Culture)
description: Hilltop Buddhist temple and centre in Itanagar, consecrated by the Dalai Lama. Features Tibetan-style architecture, white stupa, prayer wheels and panoramic views of the town and hills.
facts: Also known as Centre for Buddhist Culture or Siddhartha Vihar
Visited by the 14th Dalai Lama
Located on a hill near Nehru Museum
Offers views over Itanagar

name: Itanagar Biological Park
description: Zoological park and biological reserve about 3-4 km from Itanagar city, spanning ~250 hectares of tropical evergreen forest. Houses over 200 animals including Himalayan black bear, tiger, hornbill; first in India to breed hoolock gibbon.
facts: Started as rescue centre in 1978; relocated and renamed Biological Park
Area about 250 hectares within/near Itanagar Wildlife Sanctuary
Attracts 60,000-75,000 visitors annually
Known for successful hoolock gibbon breeding

name: Itanagar Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Protected area of about 140 sq km around Itanagar established in 1978. Tropical semi-evergreen and evergreen forests supporting tiger, leopard, clouded leopard, elephant, gaur, hornbills and diverse flora; includes Ganga Lake.
facts: Area 140.30 km², established 1978
Boundaries include Pam, Pachin rivers and streams
Home to clouded leopard, Asian elephant, gaur, hornbills
Important for environmental education near capital

name: Dikrong River (Papum Pare section)
description: Major river originating in the hills of Papum Pare district, flowing through Doimukh, Nirjuli and Banderdewa before entering Assam to join the Subansiri. Offers riverbank picnics, views and local recreation.
facts: Originates in sub-Himalayan hills of Papum Pare
Mentioned in Kalika Purana as Dikkar Basini
Flows past Doimukh and Nirjuli
Tributary of Subansiri-Brahmaputra system

name: Yupia
description: Headquarters town of Papum Pare district, about 20 km from Itanagar. Administrative centre with NIT Arunachal Pradesh campus and gateway to surrounding rural and river areas.
facts: District headquarters of Papum Pare
About 20 km from Itanagar
Home to National Institute of Technology Arunachal Pradesh
Elevation around 135-226 m

name: Doimukh
description: Small town on the banks of the Dikrong River in Papum Pare, known for scenic river views, Nyishi culture and as a local hub between Itanagar and Yupia areas.
facts: Located on Dikrong River banks
About 18 km from Yupia
PIN 791112; Nyishi community area
Scenic pebble banks and river views

name: Naharlagun
description: Major town in the Itanagar Capital Complex / Papum Pare foothills, about 10 km from Itanagar. Key transport hub with railway station connecting to the rest of India and commercial centre.
facts: Population ~36,000 (2011)
Naharlagun railway station is major railhead for Arunachal
About 10 km from Itanagar
Elevation around 155 m
